entries.statement: A manga's Wikipedia-sourced volume_boundaries rows (source 'wikipedia', grouped by manga_anilist_id|source_page) come from a page whose title-token overlap with EVERY title/title_english/synonym of the series on that manga is below 0.5.

Disposition: reported only (no auto-fix, no flag). Threshold 0.5 and the STOP-word list (line 540) are constants embedded in the class with no named rule.

entries.statement: For a manga where at least one series row has manga_status 'finished' and a known total_chapters, any Wikipedia boundary row whose chapter_start exceeds the max total_chapters across those series.
entries.notes: Second half of §10 'Volume-boundary identity + numbering space' — comment: 'for a finished manga with a known total, must not run past the total (shared pages list sequels)'. Reported only. Only applies when some series on the manga is finished (finished-only scope is a condition stated in code, not in a comment).

entries.statement: Within one manga's Wikipedia boundary set ordered by volume: (a) a row whose chapter_end is below its chapter_start, or (b) a row whose chapter_start does not exceed the previous volume's chapter_start.
bundle_parts: a boundary's end precedes its start
a boundary's start does not exceed the previous volume's start
entries.notes: Comment names the writer gate (lib/wikipedia boundariesWithDrops) and the healer (heal-volume-boundaries.ts); this is the outcome check. Disposition: reported with instruction 'run heal-volume-boundaries.ts' — not auto-fixed here. Rationale in comment: each impossible row silently mis-labels the volume of every chapter after it.

entries.statement: A series' maximum episode number exceeds max(total_episodes, max component episode_end, aired_episodes) — episodes outrun the component structure.

entries.statement: A FINISHED series whose aired_episodes exceeds its episode row count (a source counts content our episode list lacks, e.g. AFL missing a final special) — the card would promise more episodes than the list shows.

entries.statement: A series component with both episode_start and episode_end non-null where episode_start > episode_end (an unaired component must hold a NULL span, never start > end).

entries.statement: A component whose kind is set and is not 'season' and which carries an episode_start (i.e. is NUMBERED into the run) and whose 'seriesId:anilistId' key is absent from REVIEWED_NUMBERED_SPECIALS.

entries.statement: A series with resolved coverage whose largest run of canon/mixed episodes (filler and anime-only-canon excluded) strictly between consecutive anchor episodes exceeds 12 — the interpolated middle rests on nothing.

entries.notes: RESEARCH QUEUE (drives batch work-lists; §12 lines 772, 1192, 1560). entries.statement: A series with a latest anchor has one or more canon/mixed episodes numbered past that anchor's episode; these render null ch because the beyond-frontier rule refuses to extrapolate.

entries.statement: In a non-loose series, an anchor's chapter is below the previous anchor's chapter (episode order), and neither episode carries a rearranged/graft annotation.
witnesses: boruto (the ch-710 class of numbering-space junk)

Exemptions embedded: loose series skipped (borrow-maps); episodes with rearranged/graft annotations are 'settled, stop asking'.

entries.statement: In a non-loose series, an anchor's start_chapter is more than one below the previous anchor's end chapter, with no rearranged/graft annotation on either episode — a poisoned 'first chapter animated' or an unruled reorder.
entries.notes: Comment: the derive guard prevents this for AFG rows (writer side); this outcome check catches manual/wiki typos and any future writer that bypasses the guard. Ruled reorders are legal. Reported only.

entries.statement: In a non-loose series, an anchor's chapter exceeds the series' manga space — max(total_chapters, latest_known_chapters) — by more than 10.
entries.notes: Comment: 'an anchor chapter past the series' own manga space is junk by definition'; writer side is the write-time chapter-space gate (named in the anchor_nonmonotonic comment). Tolerance +10 is an embedded constant with no named rule. Reported only.

entries.statement: Against the DISPLAY total (same-edition band: latest_known_chapters when it lies in [0.8×total_chapters, total_chapters), else total_chapters): (a) an anchor chapter above it, (b) a start_chapter above it, or (c) a continue_chapter above it + 1 — a count-space value in a number-space instrument.
bundle_parts: anchor.chapter > display total
anchor.start_chapter > display total (START lives strictly inside the run)
anchor.continue_chapter > display total + 1 (CONTINUE may sit exactly one past: post_series = coverage+1)
entries.notes: Writer-side fix lives in applyMuFrontier (comment); this outcome check catches any writer. The 0.8 band mirrors assemble.ts totalChapters (comment lines 341-344) — the constant is duplicated here by hand, not imported. Reported only.

entries.statement: An anchor whose chapter is non-integer and whose source is neither 'manual' nor 'wiki' — a derived fractional anchor is a bonus/Memoire chapter mis-scraped from a source chart.

where.loc: §10 row 'Bonus/fractional chapters: record, never drop (Sean 2026-08-23, the Vanitas lesson + amendment)' (line 282)

entries.statement: An anchor from ANY source sits on an episode whose type is neither 'canon' nor 'mixed' (filler / anime-only rows never carry chapter anchors).

Healed by apply-parity-continues.ts's C3 pass — disposition 'run the parity healer', not fixed here.

where.loc: lines 154-195 (RULING VIOLATIONS + SHIFT VERIFICATION + suppressed + type overrides), 432-439 (AFG title-marker gate)

witnesses: dr-stone (ep 57/58 wore the same title after a partial heal)
bundle_parts: no episode row numbered above the community cap (COMMUNITY_COUNT_OVERRIDES; writer: filterEpisodeRows/applyCommunityCap)
aired_episodes and total_episodes never exceed the community cap
in a numbering-shifted series no two adjacent rows share a non-empty title (stale-zone signature)
in a numbering-shifted series the run is contiguous 1..max (translation never leaves holes)
a suppressed afg-continua source holds ZERO anchors on its series (CONTINUA_SUPPRESSED)
an episode's stored type equals its ruled EPISODE_TYPE_OVERRIDES value
no stored title carries AFG's '* Filler' table annotation (parser strip in lib/afg.ts since 2026-08-25)

Reported only; §12 says the class 'tripped once' (line 1372). Expected steady state 0.

entries.statement: A series with a manga source whose anchor set consists solely of source 'mu' rows — unverified by definition.

Exit: research confirms/corrects and the batch record rewrites it as source 'manual' with citations. Drains passively per batch.

entries.statement: In a non-loose series with at least two anchors, an episode annotated rearranged/graft WITH chapter data, no anchor of its own, not typed filler or anime-only-canon, and whose annotation note does not contain 'zone-acknowledged' — interpolation may paint a plausible-but-WRONG value there.
witnesses: GTO ep 20 (showed ~68 while the annotation knew 73-74; Sean's GTO 20/21 report 2026-08-23)

The 'zone-acknowledged' note marker (batch-15 rule) routes to the sibling class. §12 line 1175 says the class CLOSED (0).

entries.statement: Same predicate as rearranged_zone_unanchored but the annotation note contains 'zone-acknowledged' — research established only zone-level knowledge exists; the approximate render is accepted.
entries.notes: Acknowledged-approximate REVIEW item, 'not an open research target' (batch-15 rule per comment). The marker is a free-text substring match on episode_annotations.note — no typed column.

entries.statement: Per series: (a) zero episode rows while aired_episodes > 0 (ALL eps title_pending, canon-tier); or (b) one or more rows with null/blank title; or (c) fewer rows than aired_episodes (AFL lag — the missing eps render title_pending).
bundle_parts: series has no episode rows but aired_episodes > 0
some episode rows have empty titles
episode row count < aired_episodes
entries.notes: Comment: 'every aired episode should carry a real title (never title_pending)' — the episode-title initiative's WORK-LIST, not a defect class. Not tied to a §10 rule by the comment beyond the §12.19d agenda reference. Reported only.

entries.statement: Any episode row with a null/blank air_date, counted per series (the year line derives from episode air dates, so missing dates degrade metadata).
entries.notes: Comment names 'metadata contract, Sean 2026-08-23'. WORK-LIST for the episode-data initiative (dates come from AniList per-season start/end alongside Wikipedia titles). Reported only.

entries.statement: A series carrying any episode_annotations whose series.asterisk_review is not 'approved'. Side effect: a series with annotations and NULL asterisk_review is written to 'pending' by the audit.

where.loc: §10 rows 'Asterisk model (Sean's ruling 2026-08-23)' (line 273) and 'Asterisk review workflow (Sean 2026-08-23)' (line 276)

entries.notes: SEAN SIGN-OFF QUEUE ('pending rows are Sean's sign-off queue for the asterisk UI pass'). Comment states the rule: kinds DERIVE from episode_annotations (single source of truth); asterisk_review tracks sign-off. This class performs the only DB WRITE in audit-ui-truth (line 266, auto-heal to 'pending') — the docs (§11 line 544) describe the script as read-only.

entries.statement: A staged ingest_fractionals row with no disposition and no order-only component (episode_start null, watch_position set) sharing floor(position) in the same series — a non-main entry not yet ruled on.

entries.statement: Series with source_type 'original' or manga_status 'anime_only' — no manga instrument applies (census bucket, not a defect).

entries.statement: Series with a manga source, not loose, whose latestKnown coverage resolves (latest anchor, or finished-series synthesis from total_chapters) AND whose volume resolves (anchor volume, boundary lookup, or volume-ratio fallback) — the card renders vol + ch.
entries.notes: Census OK bucket; the §12 headline metric ('ok_full 235'). Derivation replicates buildMapping (supabaseSource.ts) by hand — see architecture entry 'lockstep'.

entries.statement: Series whose latestKnown coverage resolves but whose volume is null (no anchor volume, no boundary hit, and no total_volumes/total_chapters for the ratio fallback) — the card renders ch only.
entries.notes: Census bucket (honest degradation per CLAUDE.md invariant 4).

The rule 'LOOSE series are ruled non-linear — their anchors are borrow-maps rendered as stored; monotonicity is not a claim they make' is stated in the audit-ui-truth comment (lines 358-359) and re-stated in verify-series-display ('borrow-maps render as stored'). §12 census shows 2 loose.

entries.statement: Series with a manga source, not loose, no latestKnown, and no canon/mixed episode at all (lastCanon = 0).

entries.statement: Series with a manga source, not loose, canon episodes present, no latestKnown, and status not 'finished' (airing/upcoming with no anchor).
entries.notes: Census pending bucket; synthesis is finished-only so airing series without anchors are honestly pending.

entries.statement: Finished series with a manga source, canon episodes present, no anchor, and no total_chapters (synthesis prerequisite missing) — reported with manga_status and latest_known_chapters.

entries.statement: Residual: finished series with a manga source, canon episodes and total_chapters present but no latestKnown — should be unreachable given the synthesis rule; catches lockstep drift.
entries.notes: No comment; 'unreachable' is my reading of the branch order (finished + total_chapters + lastCanon>0 already synthesizes at line 469). Census bucket.

witnesses: MHA (sparse AFG page: stops at ep 13 of 170)

The predicate lives in lib/mu-frontier; this file only labels the result. maxChapter passed in guards MU staleness ('an MU pair that adds no chapter progress is the SAME stale frontier').

entries.statement: Series has non-MU anchors but they are stale (frontier not fresh) and MU offers no anime-coverage frontier — the card shows a truthful-but-old 'as of ep N'; files a 'count_mismatch' flag (resolve).
entries.notes: Outcome side of the anchor-freshness rule (§10 'Anchor freshness'). Comment states a rule: 'synthesis must NOT override (diverged anime would claim full coverage). Research closes these, never guesses.' Disposition: flag filed once (fileFlagOnce) + research queue.

entries.statement: Series with a manga link, no anchors, no MU frontier, and status 'airing' or 'upcoming' — honestly pending.
entries.notes: Census bucket, no flag. Counterpart of audit-ui-truth's pending_airing_no_anchor.

entries.statement: Finished anime with a publishing manga (no total_chapters), no anchors, no MU coverage, no scope — files a 'count_mismatch' flag ('needs curation').
entries.notes: Flagged + counted as 'flagged' in finishRun. Counterpart of audit-ui-truth's pending_finished_no_totals.

entries.statement: Series has a manga source_type (not original / anime_only) but no manga_anilist_id — pickManga found no ADAPTATION edge; files a 'count_mismatch' flag.
entries.notes: Flagged. No named rule; obvious from the condition (a manga-sourced series must link a manga).

entries.statement: An AFG page whose identity is ambiguous: the slug tier or full-title tier yields >1 canonical candidate and the episode span does not single one out, or the prefix tier yields candidates the span cannot disambiguate — never auto-matched.
entries.notes: SEAN-QUEUED ('reported for ruling; nothing suspicious auto-applies'). Exit = an entry in the RULED standing map. Report section 'NEEDS RULING — ambiguous identity, never auto-matched'.

entries.statement: For a matched AFG page with ≥6 episodes: AFG's max episode differs from ours by more than 2 — below ours (season-scoped page if a component boundary is within ±2, else unexplained) or above ours (unstitched newer seasons / ruled split / AFL lag — afg-extend candidate).
bundle_parts: AFG max < ours by >2 (season-scoped page vs no boundary match)
AFG max > ours by >2 (afg-extend candidate)
entries.notes: Report section labelled 'ruling material'. Sparse pages (<6 episodes or max 0) carry no signal and are skipped (constant at line 272). ±2 tolerance embedded.

entries.statement: For a matched AFG page: AFG lists N>0 seasons while we hold M>1 components and N≠M.
entries.notes: Reported only (informational). Single-component series are exempt (comps.length > 1).

entries.statement: For a matched AFG page: AFG's title (whitespace/punctuation-squashed) is not among our title / title_english / synonyms.
entries.notes: Reported only (naming axis of the three-axis cross-check).

entries.statement: An AFG page matched to a series by a non-registry tier (ruled/slug/title/prefix+span) that is not yet in series_external_ids — shown only when run without --register.

entries.notes: Count-only bucket (no ids printed).

entries.notes: OK bucket (count only).

entries.statement: A canonical series with no matched AFG page at all — no structural cross-check available.

bundle_parts: an existing afg registration is never overwritten
one afg id per series (registry constraint) — the strongest tier wins
entries.notes: Reported; both parts are refusals stated in comments ('registry constraint').

entries.statement: A staged AFL show whose served page title disagrees (titlesAgree false) with the AFL shows-index title for the same slug — an alias-corruption victim. Slugs no longer on the index are left for refresh logic (line 55). Reads the index from a fixture file, not live.

entries.statement: A series has a manga source iff source_type !== 'original' AND manga_status !== 'anime_only'; otherwise no manga instrument applies.
entries.notes: Inlined identically in both audits (and, per the lockstep comment, in supabaseSource.ts) — not a lib symbol. Candidate for the source-first typing work in system-evolution.

entries.statement: A row-less canon-tier series (no episode rows, has a manga source) defaults to canon spans, so its last canon episode is its last aired episode.
entries.notes: Comment: 'lockstep with buildMapping'. Duplicated display logic, no class of its own.

entries.statement: Coverage synthesis: with no anchor, a FINISHED series with total_chapters and at least one canon episode is taken to cover the whole manga (latestKnown = total_chapters, volume = total_volumes or ratio).
entries.notes: Replicated from buildMapping by hand. Coverage audit adds the guard: stale anchors present → synthesis must NOT override (stale_anchor_no_frontier).

entries.statement: Volume for a chapter: the boundary row containing it; else, if total_volumes and total_chapters exist, clamp(ceil(chapter × total_volumes / total_chapters), 1, total_volumes); else null.
entries.notes: Hand-copied display math (header: 'volume ratio' is one of the UI gates that can blank the display). Relates to §10 'Boundary-aware volumes everywhere'.

entries.statement: Same-edition band: for display, the chapter denominator is latest_known_chapters when it is below total_chapters but at least 0.8 × total_chapters; otherwise total_chapters.
witnesses: Kakegurui ('9' — release-derived latest was a volume count)
entries.notes: The 0.8 constant is duplicated in audit-ui-truth by hand (not imported). entries.statement: A CONTINUE point may sit exactly one chapter past the display total (post_series = coverage+1, 'you're done') but never further; a START must lie at or below the display total.
entries.notes: Stated only in this comment; checked as parts (b)/(c) of anchor_beyond_display_total.

entries.statement: A research-tier (source 'manual' or 'wiki') fractional-chapter anchor is legal — sometimes the bonus chapter IS what the episode adapts; only DERIVED fractional anchors are suspect.

entries.statement: Loose (mapping_mode 'loose') series are ruled non-linear: their anchors are borrow-maps rendered as stored, and no monotonicity, hole, or zone check applies to them.

entries.statement: AFG identity resolution proceeds by tiers — registry, then RULED, then slug equality (our id / afl_slug / slugified title), then whitespace-insensitive FULL title/synonym equality, then subtitle-stripped prefix equality (≥5 chars) — and a key claimed by two series is ambiguous and never auto-matches unless the episode span (±2 of our max or a component boundary) independently singles one out; prefix matches register ONLY with span agreement.

slug tier: AFG slug or slugified AFG title equals our id / afl_slug / slugified title
title tier: squashed full title equals any of our title / title_english / synonyms
prefix tier: colon/dash/paren-cut prefix of ≥5 chars equals one of our names — registers only when span agrees
ambiguity (>1 candidate) at any tier resolves by span agreement or is reported for ruling, never auto-matched
span agreement = within ±2 of our episode max (episodes table, else aired_episodes) or of any component episode_end

bundle_parts: The displayed chapter for a canon/mixed row is its START chapter, not its end.

Start precedence: the record's OWN start (MangaMapping.start / start_chapter) wins whenever stated (a single-chapter episode states it too); then a span's first number ('119-127' → 119); derivation only when the start is genuinely unknown (bare end value).
Derived start = previous canon episode's end + 1, clamped to this episode's own end (one derivation path off the end-position curve).

The clamp IS the majority/sliver rule: when the previous episode ended mid-chapter leaving only scraps, the next full chapter is shown; when two episodes share a chapter (end(prev) = end(ep)) the shared chapter is shown.
The first canon episode starts at the entry's scope start (mangaStartChapter), not chapter 1.
Across a reorder boundary (different regime, or prevEnd > end) no start is derived → null; callers fall back to the row's own end value when one is known.
entries.notes: Rendering the start requires the ambiguity fix in MangaMapping.start (Sean's Gintama ep-35 report, 2026-08-24: an exact ch-86 record rendered as ch 48 because derivation walked backwards into a jumped block). The 'sliver' language does not appear in this home; the client calls it 'the majority rule'. WITNESSED by tests: mapping.position.test.ts 'canonEpStartCh — display shows the FIRST chapter animated' → 'derives start as the previous episode's end + 1', 'clamps the start to this episode's own end when both share a chapter', 'starts the first episode at the entry's scope start, not chapter 1'.

entries.statement: solvePosition — the unified position solve: one driver field (ep | vol | ch) resolves to a full position whose state is 'run' (aired), 'hatch' (manga_only tail) or 'out' (out_of_range), with filler/anime-only episodes carrying NO manga values.
bundle_parts: A non-integer or < 1 query value yields null (pending), not a fabricated position.
ch < scope start → 'out' with boundMsg 'ch {startCh}-{published}' (chapters before the scope belong to a predecessor series).
ch > published → 'out' with the same boundMsg and unit = aired + aheadUnits + 1.
ch ≤ covered → 'run': the episode whose confirmed chapter range contains ch wins; otherwise chToEp; type from the exact row else episodeTypeAt.
covered < ch ≤ published → 'hatch' with a unit proportional to the tail's pacing (aired when no tail).
ep ≤ aired and type filler or anime-only-canon → 'run' with noManga = true (vol/ch null by design).
ep ≤ aired with an exact record → START chapter per the first-chapter ruling; vol from chToVol(start) falling back to the record's volume.
ep ≤ aired without a record → canonEpStartCh estimate (null when none) and its volume.
ep > aired → 'hatch' projection when a tail exists and the projected chapter ≤ published; otherwise 'out' with boundMsg 'ep 1-{aired}'.
vol < scope start volume or > totalVolumes → 'out' with boundMsg 'vol {startVol}-{totalVolumes ?? ?}'; without a per-volume ratio → null.
vol → resolves as the volume's FIRST chapter (volStartCh) with chEnd = the volume's estimated last chapter, then solves as a chapter.
entries.notes: Interaction spec is cited as docs/components/map-lookup.md (not read; outside the brief). Vol-driven chapter resolution uses the ratio (perVol) even when volume boundaries exist — a second inconsistency with the boundaries-first rule (chToVol is boundaries-first, the vol→ch inverse is ratio-only).

From outside the range, stepping toward it snaps to the boundary and stepping away is a no-op.

entries.statement: AFG episode-numbering conversion: AFG counts in MAL-style numbering, so the claimed frontier episode is shifted past every non-season numbered component (insert) that starts at or before it — unless the page's own chart max already reaches our aired count (already in our space); a converted episode above aired_episodes is discarded and the pin falls back to the run end.
witnesses: Haikyu (Riku vs Kuu = our eps 61-62; AFG ep 85 = our 87)

skip conversion when afgPageMax >= aired_episodes

no episode at all → 'no_data'

entries.statement: A1 at the AFG continua writer (D4): filler and anime-only rows NEVER take anchors — a continua end-frontier landing on an episode whose type is not canon/mixed is refused with a count_mismatch flag (allow-list, unknown types fail closed; a row-less episode cannot be typed so the pin stands); the continue-from chapter still applies because it is reading guidance, not a position.

entries.statement: Continua precedence at the (series, episode) PK: a manual or wiki anchor at the pin episode is never overwritten (continua cross-checks it — disagreement > 1 chapter files a count_mismatch flag, curated kept); a chart-'afg' or 'mu' anchor yields to the curated continua (disagreement > 2 flags, then continua is applied).
bundle_parts: manual/wiki holder → kept_curated; |diff| > 1 flags
afg/mu holder → continua wins; |diff| > 2 flags
entries.notes: Tier order implied: manual/wiki > afg-continua > afg (chart) / mu. Sources verify each other in conjunction; none limits another.

entries.statement: Parity-continue preservation (C2): continue_chapter/continue_kind/continue_note are curated data that may live on derived rows, so every delete+reinsert rebuild of 'afg' or 'afg-continua' anchors carries them over by episode — otherwise the hourly cron erodes the catalog-wide parity conversion one series at a time.
entries.notes: For continua the continue fields are restored only when the fresh pin lands on the SAME episode as the old one. NOT applied to 'mu' rows (applyMuFrontier deletes without snapshotting continue fields) — possible gap.

entries.statement: Three-numbers model: the explicit continue-from chapter is data of its own (it may skip recaps or backtrack) and is never derived as frontier+1; the continua source owns series.continue_from_chapter ONLY where it owns the frontier — where manual/wiki rule the frontier, research rules the continue point too. Exception: on an A1 refusal the continue-from is still written.
entries.notes: Note the tension: the D4 refusal branch writes continue_from_chapter even though continua did NOT get the frontier — the 'owns it only where it owns the frontier' principle has a stated exception (reading guidance still applies).

entries.statement: Continua volume boundary: written only when absent for (manga, volume); an existing (Wikipedia-staged) boundary that disagrees is not overwritten but files a count_mismatch flag ('verify which edition').
entries.notes: Requires manga_anilist_id and all three of continueVolume/volumeStart/volumeEnd.

entries.statement: AFG numbering alignment: when the AFG page's max episode differs from our max episode by more than 12, the whole page's anchors are withheld with a count_mismatch flag.
entries.notes: Only when we already have episode rows (ourMax truthy). Compares SOURCE-space afgMax against our max BEFORE translation — for shift-ruled series the gap is the insert length (fine under 12).

entries.statement: Chapter-space gate (chart): if any derived AFG chart anchor exceeds max(total_chapters, latest_known_chapters) + 10, the whole page's numbering is suspect (franchise-continuous numbering) — all anchors withheld with a parse_integrity flag, never partially written.
entries.notes: Boruto has 81 chapters; AFG rows said 702-710 (Naruto-space).

entries.statement: Derived-anchor precedence (HxH ep-140 lesson): the PK allows one anchor per episode, so derived 'afg' chart rows at episodes holding a manual/wiki (research-tier) anchor are dropped — curated rows always win on every refresh.
entries.notes: 'completed 2026-08-23'.

entries.statement: Chart anchors translate episode numbers through the source-numbering shifts (space 'afg') exactly like episode rows; dropped order-only entries never anchor.

entries.statement: A1 at the AFG chart writer (D4): derived chart anchors on rows typed anything other than canon/mixed are dropped (allow-list; row-less episodes pass) — AFG's chapter column is a reading-position CONVERSION that plateaus across noncanon rows, so a chart value on a noncanon row is a conversion artifact, not an adaptation claim.
witnesses: one-piece (eps 214/216 both print 313 on rows AFG marks *Filler)
entries.notes: Comment names the outcome audit: anchor_on_noncanon_row. The type lookup reads ALL episode rows for the series with an unpaged select — see the 1000-row-cap architecture entry in part 4.

entries.statement: Curated-consistency (Boruto ep-219 lesson): a derived chart row whose chapter contradicts the ordering around any research-tier anchor (chapter above a later curated anchor, or below an earlier one) is chart imprecision — the ruling wins and the derived row drops; ruled rearrangements live as annotations, never as derived rows.
entries.notes: Equal chapter at a different episode is allowed (<= / >=). The 'live as annotations' half is a process statement, not enforced here.

entries.statement: Bonus/fractional chapters a chart associates with an episode are never silently dropped: they become 'graft' episode_annotations, FILL-ONLY (research-tier annotations at the same episode+kind are never clobbered), and set the series' asterisk_review to 'pending' when null.
entries.notes: 'we must always know what content makes up an episode'. A research-verified fractional anchor MAY be written at the manual tier when the bonus IS what the episode adapts.

entries.statement: A successful chart sync registers the afg external id and dismisses every open 'afg' ingest flag for that slug.
entries.notes: Dismisses by series_key = afgSlug and source 'afg' regardless of flag kind.

entries.statement: Volumes-staleness event: when the highest derived anchor chapter passes the last known volume boundary start by more than 20, a 'wikipedia' count_mismatch flag on manga:<id> asks for a volumes re-ingest — the validation tier is event-driven, never scheduled.
entries.notes: Math.max over an empty rows array yields -Infinity, so no flag when nothing was written.

entries.statement: MU's anime-coverage field is multi-segment prose: parse ALL 'Vol N, Chap M' pairs and trust an explicit 'EP N' pin only when the text holds exactly one pair.
witnesses: Naruto (EP number belonging to the Boruto clause)

entries.statement: 'mu' anchors are derivations: applying the MU frontier first DELETES the series' existing 'mu' anchor and re-derives it, so rule fixes heal everything on the next pass; a suppressed series stops after the delete.
entries.notes: Matches CLAUDE.md invariant 7 (repairs on derivation-tier rows are deleted by the next re-derive).

entries.statement: Sibling-scope ceiling (D1): when sibling entries share the same manga, the smallest sibling manga_start_chapter above this entry's own start bounds this entry from above; MU pairs at or past the ceiling are out of scope and filtered; if every in-band pair is past the ceiling the frontier is withheld with a count_mismatch flag (refused_sibling_scope).
entries.notes: The batch-17 franchise-conflation class. Filtering rather than refusing lets the multi-segment parse pick this entry's own labeled endpoint.

entries.statement: MU scope band: only coverage pairs within [manga_start_chapter ?? 1, total_chapters ?? ∞] are candidates; the largest in-scope pair is the coverage.
entries.notes: Scope start comes from series_scopes via manga_start_chapter.

entries.statement: Chapter-space gate (MU pins): MU's coverage prose describes the whole franchise, so a pin above max(total_chapters, latest_known_chapters) + 10 is a structure/edition mismatch — withheld with a count_mismatch flag (out_of_space), never written.

Count-space → number-space conversion (Tokyo Ghoul 144/143): for a finished manga where AniList's total is a COUNT and MU's latest is the last chapter NUMBER (same-edition band: latest < total and latest ≥ 80% of total), an MU pin that lands between them is count-space and is converted to the latest number, so the position never renders coverage above its own denominator; mirrors the display rule in assemble.ts totalChapters exactly.
entries.notes: Writer copy here; display copy in src/data/catalog/assemble.ts totalChapters (client home). The conversion is recorded in the anchor note.

entries.statement: Airing-pin rule (TYBW): without an explicit episode in MU's text the pin would land at the run end, a moving target while airing — so MU frontier pins apply to FINISHED runs only; airing series need the explicit episode or a research anchor.
witnesses: Bleach TYBW (ch 705 announced while part 4 mid-air)
entries.notes: Returns 'no_coverage' silently (no flag). Applies only when the caller passes status; status undefined bypasses the rule.

entries.statement: MU pin episode = the explicit EP when it is ≤ aired_episodes, else the run end (aired_episodes).

MU pin redundancy keys on the PIN EPISODE, never a freshness window or chapter no-progress: the pin is skipped only when a non-MU anchor already covers the pin episode itself (nonMuMaxEp ≥ pin episode).
entries.notes: SUPERSEDES the old 'non-MU anchors within 12 eps of the run end' blanket skip and the chapter no-progress skip (both recorded as pipeline traps in part 4). Rationale: the beyond-frontier display rule refuses to extrapolate past the last anchor, so 'fresh enough' ≠ 'covers the run end'.

entries.statement: Curated precedence at the MU pin episode: any non-'mu' anchor already at the pin episode IS the frontier — the MU pin is skipped (one-anchor-per-episode PK rule).
entries.notes: Broader than manual/wiki: any non-mu source (afg, afg-continua) at the pin episode wins over MU.

entries.statement: Scope-consumed refusal (D1): when non-MU anchors already reach the END of this entry's chapter scope (min(total_chapters, sibling ceiling − 1)) yet the MU pin episode extends beyond all research, the trailing episodes cannot adapt this scope — the frontier is withheld with a count_mismatch flag (refused_scope_consumed); placed after the redundancy skips so a fully-researched series stays a silent skip.

entries.statement: A1 at the MU writer (D1): a run-end MU pin landing on an episode whose type is not canon/mixed is refused with a count_mismatch flag (allow-list; row-less episodes pass so synthesized-row entries keep their frontier); research records the honest terminal on the last canon/mixed episode instead.
entries.notes: The original A1-at-writer gate; D4 (2026-08-25) extended it to both AFG writers.

entries.statement: Same-edition band: MU's latest_chapter is accepted only when 0 < latest < 10000 and, when an AniList count exists, latest ≥ 80% of that count — below the band the two sources track different editions and callers flag, never write.
entries.notes: MU latest_chapter is release-record-derived: reliable for currently scanlated manga, garbage for old completed ones.

entries.statement: Chapter-floor (symmetric to the episode-floor invariant): the chapter space can never be smaller than what confirmed anchors reach — an MU latest below the anchor floor is a different unit space (volumes), never a chapter number, and is rejected.

Best-available latest_known: release-derived latest_chapter first, then the chapter count parsed from MU's status string ('67 Chapters (Ongoing)') as fallback — both behind the same-edition band AND the anchor chapter floor; this is the one derivation every writer uses.
entries.alias: Sean's standing rule (use the best info available)
entries.notes: Consumers: mu-backfill, audit-manga-coverage, apply-rulings-20260825b, refresh-mu.

entries.statement: MU publication status: the explicit completed=true flag wins (finished); else the FIRST line of the status string maps complete→finished, hiatus→hiatus, ongoing→publishing; else completed===false → publishing; else null.
entries.notes: Multi-part status strings state the overall status on line 1.

entries.statement: Manga-status cross-check: MU's publication status is an independent statement; disagreement with our AniList-derived manga_status files a taxonomy_conflict flag for review and NEVER auto-applies; skipped when ours is anime_only or MU has no status.

entries.statement: Ownership guard: a chain walk never crosses into an AniList entry already claimed by another canonical series (series.anilist_id or series_components.anilist_id), so deliberate splits are safe by construction whatever a source's continuous numbering suggests.

derivative-manga rule on the head

entries.statement: Component spans: a component with nothing aired holds NO span (episode_start/end null — a 0-length entry would produce start > end); episode_end is set only when the total is known or the component is airing; kind derives from format (MOVIE→movie, OVA→ova, SPECIAL→special, else season); in-flow extras (Kizumonogatari pattern) are written with null ranges after the component they follow.

entries.statement: AFG chapters-cell parse: ', ' or ';' separate entries while bare commas are thousands separators ('1,144'); ranges 'a-b' / 'a–b' / 'a to b' expand only when b ≥ a and the span is under 500; decimals are kept (bonus chapters); values ≤ 0 or ≥ 10000 are parse artifacts and dropped.
entries.notes: 'no manga has 10k chapters'.

entries.statement: AFG page parse guards: single-cell divider lines ('<—— Pelicula 2 ——>') never become the running arc label; header rows skipped; the episode cell must be strictly 'N.' (1-4 digits) so summary/colspan rows never digit-concatenate into fake numbers; placeholder title cells like '(01).' normalize to an empty (pending) title; AFG's '* Filler' marker inside the title cell is stripped (it is annotation, not the name); type comes from the number cell's class (red=filler, blue=mixed, else canon); an episode repeated across tables keeps its first occurrence.
bundle_parts: divider rows are not arc labels (Naruto 6-27 regression)
episode cell strictly /^\d{1,4}\.?$/
placeholder title '(01).' → '' (Sean's Dorohedoro report)
strip trailing '* Filler' from title (Sean's eyeshield report)
type from td class red/blue
dedupe by first occurrence
entries.notes: Watch-order surfacing is the fractional pipeline's job, not the arc field's.

entries.statement: Canonical adaptation-list serialization: chapters_adapted is comma-separated, consecutive integer runs compressed to ranges, ORDER PRESERVED AS ADAPTED (never sorted), fractional values kept inline.
entries.notes: c3.ts parses this format back (strips parentheticals, extracts integers).

entries.statement: Derived AFG anchor per row: the position (end) chapter is the highest MAINLINE (integer) chapter, the start is the first mainline chapter (real source data — display anchors at starts), fractional values are bonus entries and never drive position, and a bonus-only row yields no anchor (research's call).
entries.notes: start_chapter captured at the writer rather than re-derived by formula downstream.

entries.statement: Anchor monotonicity / spike filter: chapters never decrease as episodes advance, so derived anchors keep only the longest non-decreasing chapter subsequence — stray values (divider digits merged into a row, flash-forward grafts) are outliers against the chart's own trend and drop, without the old arc-pattern guard that nuked whole stretches.
entries.notes: Supersedes the arc-pattern guard (Naruto 6-27 regression).

entries.statement: Start sanity (Oshi ep-4): a derived row's start is recomputed as the lowest mainline chapter that is ≥ the previous kept row's end and ≤ its own end (a split chapter is shared — equal is legal; a start one BELOW the previous end is chart double-listing noise, not data); off-trend values stay recorded in chapters_adapted; research-tier starts are exempt.
witnesses: Oshi no Ko (ep 4 listed a stray 10 beside 17-19)
entries.notes: The audit class name anchor_start_offtrend is cited by CONTINUA_SUPPRESSED (resolve.ts line 118), not here; linking it is an inference for the merge to confirm.

entries.statement: Continua parse: the heading is captured (never trusted blindly); frontier episode taken from 'ended at episode N' (absolute) or from 'last canon episode … is Nth of Season S' only when S is 1 or absent (season-relative numbers are not absolute); frontier chapter = max of the 'corresponds to Chapters …' list; continue chapter from 'start reading from Chapter N'; volume + collected range from 'Volume V (collects chapters a to b)'.
entries.notes: Comment: 'Wikipedia + research stay co-verifiers everywhere (Sean: AFG coverage never limits the other sources)' — comment-only principle.

entries.statement: AFL page integrity: the page states its data twice (episode table and Quick List, both semantically classed); per type the table's episode set must equal the Quick List's, and mismatches are reported so the caller refuses the page (parse_integrity).
entries.notes: lib computes integrity.ok; the refusal itself lives in callers (stageAfl does NOT check page.integrity — verify in the scripts/edge homes where it is checked).

entries.statement: AFL row parse: episode 0 is real (OVAs/prologues) and only negative numbers are rejected; duplicate rows with the same number AND type collapse to one, while same-number rows with differing types are kept so the integrity check flags the page instead of silently picking a side; canonicalSlug is read from the first episode link for the alias-corruption check.
bundle_parts: episode 0 accepted, negatives rejected
dedupe same number+type only
canonicalSlug from first td.Title link

entries.statement: Wikipedia volume boundaries: volume N spans [its first chapter start .. next volume's first start − 1]; the final volume stays open (null end).

Monotonic-start gate: chapter starts must strictly increase with volume number; a volume whose start is ≤ the previous kept start is a parse artifact, is DROPPED, and the remaining rows re-close around the gap (a slightly coarser self-consistent table beats a precise-looking contradictory one — the Ippo v61 partial-boundary principle); dropped rows are returned so callers can flag the manga for research.
witnesses: Sailor Moon (v3 'chs 10-3'; 24 rows across 11 manga were live)
entries.notes: Consumers: volumes-backfill, heal-volume-boundaries, audit-ui-truth; toBoundaries (drop-blind) used only by parser-check.

entries.statement: Wikipedia fractional episode numbers (35.5, 13.5, 0.5) are the community convention for specials/OVAs/movies slotted BETWEEN episodes without being counted — exactly our order-only concept; their presence proves the page shares our numbering space; they may describe order-only components but are never episode rows.
entries.notes: comment-only in lib: parseEpisodeList returns fractional numbers unchanged; the caller (wiki-episodes-backfill) must exclude them. Related: mashle 6.5 fractional ruling 2026-08-25.

entries.statement: Wikipedia page discovery: prefix-search 'List of X chapters|episodes' families first; the full-text fallback accepts a hit only when its inner title shares ≥ 50% tokens with a candidate title — search ranking alone is not identity.
witnesses: My Dress-Up Darling (search once returned 'List of Ranma ½ chapters')
entries.notes: findEpisodePages duplicates findChapterPages verbatim (two copies of the same token-agreement logic; a third copy is resolve.ts#titlesAgree with stop-words).

entries.statement: Wikipedia episode-list parse: the overall EpisodeNumber is preferred; a lone EpisodeNumber on a season page may be season-relative and the CALLER's alignment gate decides trustworthiness; rows dedupe by number (first occurrence wins); transclusion targets ({{:Page}}) are extracted for depth-1 follow because main lists often hold only season markers.
witnesses: dr-stone (list holds only {{:Dr. Stone season N}} markers)
entries.notes: Episode-data initiative §12.19d. The alignment gate is NOT in lib.

entries.statement: AFL slug → AniList id matching runs in confidence order — source_map (including manual overrides, method 'manual') → AniFiller seed (confidence 1.0, verified) → exact title match (0.95) → synonym match (0.85) — and anything ambiguous files a match_ambiguous flag and matches NOTHING; guessing is what the flag queue exists to prevent.

AniFiller seed = fact only, never its episode data (unlicensed)
exact title over romaji/english/native, series formats (TV/TV_SHORT/ONA) outrank on ties
synonym match
ambiguous → flag, null

entries.statement: One AniList id per AFL slug: if persisting a match hits the unique constraint because another AFL slug already owns the AniList id, the match is refused and a match_ambiguous flag names the owner — two AFL pages for one series needs a merge ruling.

entries.statement: C3 skip-note predicate: a continue point sitting STRICTLY below chapters the same episode already covered must carry a note telling the reader which chapters to skip on arrival; continue == an adapted chapter is C1 (mid-chapter straddle, re-reading intended, never 'skip'); parenthesized page/graft facts in chapters_adapted are stripped before number extraction so page spans never masquerade as chapters; fractional chapters are ignored.
bundle_parts: ahead = integer chapters in chapters_adapted strictly > continue_chapter
skip language = /skip|already|covered|re-read/i
note stamp format 'C3 (Sean 2026-08-25): … skip on arrival unless re-reading.' capped at 600 chars

Note the healer lives under research/batch15/, not scripts/ingest/ proper. 'both' here = writer (healer) + audit, not display.

entries.statement: For recurring conditions a flag is filed only when no OPEN flag of the same kind already exists for the series key (fileFlagOnce); fileFlag always inserts. A flag records the anomaly AND the proposed data so it can be ruled on later without re-scraping; callers HOLD the change.

Everything lands raw in staging; promotion is the resolver's decision.

AFL/AFG 10s per-host floor + conditional GET

placeholder titles
'* Filler' in title

entries.statement: AFG numbers episodes MAL-style (excluding community-numbered mid-run inserts) — so a continua 'ended at episode N' can be N+inserts in our space; and AFG's continua template can name a DIFFERENT series (SHY/Kamonohashi Ron, Cuckoos/Dandadan); and a continua episode can sit one short of the page's own chart rows (you-and-i-are-polar-opposites).

side-story PREQUEL
missing source
0-aired span
recap-inflated counts

rating churn → muHash

entries.statement: Wikipedia traps: a mis-parsed volume start silently corrupts every downstream boundary (Sailor Moon v3 'chs 10-3'); full-text search ranking returns the wrong series (Ranma ½ for My Dress-Up Darling); episode lists live on transcluded season pages (Dr. Stone); chapter lists come in three dialects ({{Numbered list|start}}, <li value>, bare range with a series label like 'Mission: 1–5'); smart-quote entities in AFG headings.

entries.statement: Pipeline traps (superseded designs recorded in comments): a bare DB update on a derived row is clobbered by the next refresh (hence maps that re-apply); the old 'non-MU anchor within 12 eps of run end' freshness skip and the chapter no-progress skip deleted real run-end pins (AoT ep 89, Kuroko 75, Naruto 220); the old arc-pattern anchor guard nuked whole stretches when a divider propagated as arc (Naruto 6-27); same-episode precedence cannot stop a wrong source value landing on a different episode (Claymore/Kimi); the hourly cron erodes curated continue fields on derived rows unless carried over (C2); an import that takes AFG titles but never maps its filler flag defaults every row canon (eyeshield-21); deleting to the source-space max eats rows the translation does not refill (Ryuusui); a drop-only shift lets a renumbered extra re-enter (yu-yu-hakusho 113).

entries.statement: Consolidation principle: rules live in shared lib code consumed identically by scripts and edge functions; rulings are declarative records; audits verify OUTCOMES so a misbehaving writer surfaces as data; incomplete inputs degrade gracefully, never into garbage; nothing is presented to Sean unresearched.
bundle_parts: rules live in shared lib code consumed identically by scripts and edge functions
rulings are declarative records
audits verify OUTCOMES so a misbehaving writer surfaces as data
incomplete inputs degrade gracefully, never into garbage
nothing is presented to Sean unresearched
entries.notes: Restates CLAUDE.md hard invariants 1, 3, 4, 5 in one paragraph ('Sean's standing directive, systematized').

entries.statement: Two consolidate modes: `/consolidate` = steps 1-8; `/consolidate deep` = steps 1-8 plus step 9 (full-catalog rescan against current rules, notes re-validated, stale cleanup). Run deep without being asked when a rule change plausibly invalidates prior per-series decisions, and say so. Expect deep often while the data logic is under active design, tapering as it stabilizes.
entries.notes: apply-batch restates the trigger as: did this batch change a RULE (writer gate, lib behaviour, typing ruling)? → offer deep, not plain. CLAUDE.md cycle step 6 also carries it. Header flags the trigger as 'judgment-heavy' and slated for rework.

The crons must run the same code as the scripts — always.

Step 4 healer roster (all idempotent), run in order: afg-continua-apply.ts; audit-manga-coverage.ts; cleanup-flags.ts; heal-volume-boundaries.ts (MONOTONIC-START rule); research/batch15/apply-parity-continues.ts (ANIME-PARITY continue points, C2); then re-run `resolveSeries` for affected series if numbering/type rulings changed (stale-zone healing removes stranded rows).

entries.statement: Step 8 save point: update memory file (mangamapper-data-sources.md) as a REFRESH POINT (current census, new rules, open queues, next steps); commit with a message that reads as the ruling record; push to main (Vercel deploys from main); report the census delta and any items awaiting Sean.

Deep rescan — notes are precedence, not blindfolds: rulings, suppressions, overrides, closed flags and 'don't touch' notes are still SCANNED and respected as the default, but re-checked: note blocks something no longer valid → bring to Sean with evidence; change is clear-cut under an established rule → disregard the note, apply, update the note to record the supersession, REPORT (never silently); ambiguous → flag, research first, present a verdict.

entries.statement: Deep rescan stale cleanup: delete no-longer-referenced logic (dead constants, ruling entries pointing at series/episodes that no longer exist, orphaned staging rows, resolved-but-lingering flags, dead scripts); every deletion is listed in the report.

Permanence tiers: a series that is FINISHED and FULLY PUBLISHED, with its mapping researched, cross-verified and Sean-signed, is effectively LOCKED — its decisions are permanent and it drops out of routine deep rescans, revisited only when a rule change explicitly touches it; airing/ongoing/unverified series stay in the active rescan pool.
entries.notes: No lock mechanism (flag/column) is named — text describes a goal state; whether a locked set exists in data is for the lib/scripts homes.

entries.statement: Close the loop (every consolidate pass): Capture — for each finding name where it was routed per CLAUDE.md's capture table (§10 rule + writer gate + audit class, an agent/skill trap, a curated map, or a §12 entry); Check the gates are real — every §10 rule should have an enforcement site AND an outcome check, and a rule with no audit class is a candidate for automation; Report cycle position — say where the project sits in the data cycle and what step is next.

check gates are real: enforcement site AND outcome check per rule; no audit class = automation candidate
report cycle position and next step
entries.notes: apply-batch adds: 'If nothing was learned, say that — a legitimate outcome and better than inventing one.'

entries.statement: Anything an agent proposes that is not in a curated map gets REPORTED, not applied.

Curated continues carry continue_kind + continue_note and are never overwritten by the parity healer (which fills only absent metadata).

unknown → furthest+1 with annotation

entries.statement: Batch-14-lineage anchor normalizers (copied verbatim in batches 14/15/16/17): SLIVER RULE — the episode's START is the first chapter animated; a leading PARTIAL of the IMMEDIATELY preceding chapter counts unless it is scraps (≤5 pages, or sliver/teaser/cold-open/fragment/panel/scrap/recap/flashback/montage/preview/replay wording); a far-earlier chapter opening the episode is a relocated graft and never the position (AoT ep 87). RUNNING-ORDER END — END is the POSITION instrument: when the agent's end sits below the start, lift END to the highest integer chapter in the adapted list (Dagashi S1 '58, 32, 15').
bundle_parts: START = first chapter animated
leading partial of prev chapter counts unless ≤5 pages / scrappy wording
far-earlier opener is a graft, never position
END lifted to max integer chapter when end < start
entries.notes: Four identical copies; a rule that lives at call sites (violates invariant 1). Regex-based page counting is the mechanical form of the ≤5-page threshold.

entries.statement: Batch-14-lineage apply contract: anchors upsert chapter + start_chapter + chapters_adapted + volume with source 'manual' and a batch-tagged note; an anchor whose episode > aired, start > end, or duplicated in the verdict is skipped; an END more than 10 past the current chapter space is noted (research sets the floor; latest_known heals via MU); REPAIRS of existing non-mu curated values are DETECTED and printed, never silent; a mu pin replaced by manual prints '(verified)' or '(REPLACED)'; continue points require an anchor; annotations upsert on (series, episode, kind) and set asterisk_review 'pending'; type corrections apply only when EPISODE_TYPE_OVERRIDES already carries them (a bare DB retype would be clobbered by the next AFL refresh) — missing ones print as TODO; agents' flags_for_sean become ONE review bookmark flag per series; order-only records need adaptation spans and are matched by title tokens against existing fractionals (never duplicated), position = the `after` component's end + .1/.2… (Ippo 76.3/76.6 precedent).
bundle_parts: full-record upsert, source manual
skip: ep>aired, start>end, duplicate ep
chapter-space +10 note
REPAIR detection printed never silent
continue requires anchor
annotations → asterisk pending
type corrections only via EPISODE_TYPE_OVERRIDES
one bookmark per series
order-only: spans required, title-token dedup, after-end + .1

bundle_parts: zone-ack marker after annotations
annotation_updates upsert
repairs only via REPAIRS_APPROVED
EXCLUDED_ANCHORS withholding
